question: A straight chain of three carbon atoms having no double bond and -OH functional group at first carbon atom is named:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Propanol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The name of an organic compound is determined by the number of **carbon atoms** in its longest chain. A chain with **three carbon atoms** uses the prefix **Prop-**.
 
• The description "having no double bond" indicates that the compound is **saturated**. In chemical nomenclature, saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) use the primary suffix **-ane**. When a functional group is added, the 'e' is typically dropped, making the base name **Propan-**.
 
• The presence of an **-OH functional group** identifies the molecule as an **alcohol**. According to **IUPAC nomenclature**, alcohols are designated by the suffix **-ol**.
 
• The location of the functional group is specified by numbering the carbon chain. Since the **hydroxyl group (-OH)** is at the **first carbon atom**, the systematic name is **Propan-1-ol**, commonly referred to as **Propanol**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Propanol.***
 
• **Evaluating other options:**
 
 
• **Propanone**: This is a **ketone** (suffix **-one**) which requires a **carbonyl group (C=O)** on a non-terminal carbon. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Propane**: This is a simple **alkane** consisting only of carbon and hydrogen with no functional groups like **-OH**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Propanal**: This is an **aldehyde** (suffix **-al**) which contains a **-CHO group** at the end of the chain rather than an **-OH group**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature System**: This is a globally recognized method of naming organic chemical compounds maintained by the **International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry**. It ensures that every compound has a unique and unambiguous name based on its **molecular structure**.
 
• **Root Word Selection**: The prefix is determined by the number of carbons: **Meth- (1)**, **Eth- (2)**, **Prop- (3)**, **But- (4)**, **Pent- (5)**, and **Hex- (6)**. For this question, **three carbons** lead directly to **Prop-**.
 
• **Functional Group Suffixes**:
 
 
• **Alcohols (-OH)**: Use the suffix **-ol**. Example: **Methanol** (CH3OH).
 
• **Aldehydes (-CHO)**: Use the suffix **-al**. Example: **Ethanal** (CH3CHO).
 
• **Ketones (>C=O)**: Use the suffix **-one**. Example: **Butanone** (CH3COCH2CH3).
 
• **Carboxylic Acids (-COOH)**: Use the suffix **-oic acid**. Example: **Ethanoic acid** (CH3COOH).
 
 
 
• **Saturated vs. Unsaturated**: A **saturated** compound contains only **single bonds** between carbon atoms, whereas **unsaturated** compounds contain at least one **double bond** (alkenes, suffix **-ene**) or **triple bond** (alkynes, suffix **-yne**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structure of Propanol**: The chemical formula for **Propan-1-ol** is **C3H8O**, often written as **CH3CH2CH2OH** to show the straight-chain structure.
 
• **Isomerism**: Propanol has a structural isomer called **Propan-2-ol** (commonly known as **Isopropyl alcohol** or **Isopropanol**), where the **-OH group** is attached to the **second carbon atom** instead of the first.
 
• **Physical Properties**: **Propan-1-ol** is a colorless liquid at **room temperature** and is used extensively as a **solvent** in the pharmaceutical industry and for making **antiseptics**.
 
• **Classification**: It is classified as a **primary alcohol** because the carbon atom holding the **hydroxyl group** is attached to only **one other carbon atom**.
